newsitem.title: USA: C-TEC hits year high after IRS ruling on spin-off.
newsitem.headline: C-TEC hits year high after IRS ruling on spin-off.

text.p: Shares in C-TEC Corp rose to a new year high on Wednesday after the U.S. Internal Revenue Service approved company plans for a tax-free spin-off into three separate, publicly traded companies.
C-TEC was up 1-7/8 to 33-1/8 in late afternoon trading. Its previous year high was 32.

C-TEC's RCN unit, which would become a separate telecommunications company under the spin-off proposal, on Wednesday began running full-page print advertisements in Boston and New York, offering cable, Internet and local and long-distance telephone service to residential customers.
C-TEC last month reported a first-quarter loss of $0.27 per share, and chairman and chief executive, David McCourt, said RCN would not immediately be profitable on its own.
"You'll have losses at RCN while we're building network," McCourt said.
After the spin-off, McCourt will become chairman and chief executive of RCN, which he said plans to challenge cable and local-phone companies.
McCourt said RCN already has 50,000 customers in Boston and New York and plans to acquire more with its year-long, $10 million ad campaign, which includes television spots.
He said the company is building an $8 billion fiber-optic network that eventually will stretch from Boston to Washington.
All three C-TEC spin-offs are to be traded publicly, probably on Nasdaq.
C-TEC's cable operations in Michigan and local telephone operations in Pennsylvania also are to be spun off to shareholders, in a deal expected to close by year's end.
